usds-sky.title: How does USDS break?
usds-sky.thesis: A coalition that captures governance and survives the 48-hour notice period can mint unbacked USDS or replace its logic; LitePSM exits remain inventory-limited.
usds-sky.premise: Hypothetical: a coalition outvotes Sky's governing address, queues a harmful spell, and prevents a defensive replacement from cancelling it before execution. No capture or misconduct is alleged. Unless stated otherwise, measurements and fork replays use block 26,139,200 on 2026-10-07. The exit calculation assumes unchanged contracts, funded and approved callers, no replenishment and no competing withdrawals; it covers only LitePSM inventory, not other venues or future prices. Collateral-book figures are DAO-wide and shared with DAI, not USDS-only reserves.

stages.title: Outvote the sitting hat
stages.action: Lock SKY in the Chief, vote for a slate carrying one spell contract, then lift it
stages.cost: SKY voting weight is escrowed, not spent
stages.explanation: The Chief authorises the current governing address, called the hat, and lift replaces it only with a candidate holding strictly more SKY approvals. The pinned hat had 7.04bn SKY approvals, 30.0% of SKY supply; this moving weight is informational, and lift permits replacements in the last lift's block or after more than 10 blocks.

stages.title: Queue one spell
stages.action: DSPause.plot(spell, codehash, calldata, eta) with eta at or after now + 172800
stages.cost: One transaction from the hat
stages.explanation: Only the current hat can queue a plan through the recorded Chief-to-Pause route. On the pinned fork, a non-hat call and a hat call scheduled one second too early reverted, while scheduling exactly 172,800 seconds ahead succeeded.

stages.title: Wait out 48 hours
stages.action: The queued plan sits in DSPause.plans until its eta
stages.cost: Two days of public notice
stages.explanation: Cancellation belongs to the current hat, so voters can stop the plan by electing a defensive replacement that calls drop before execution. The route assumes they fail; the replay rejected execution one second early and allowed it exactly 172,800 seconds after plotting.

stages.title: Execute the spell
stages.action: DSPause.exec(spell, codehash, calldata, eta)
stages.cost: One transaction, and any address may send it
stages.explanation: Anyone can execute an uncancelled plan after its scheduled time if the target codehash still matches; the replay used an unrelated caller. The spell runs inside PauseProxy, whose external token calls carry the governor's authority, and execution requires its owner to remain DSPause.

stages.title: Mint or replace USDS
stages.action: Usds.rely(newMinter) then Usds.mint(to, amount), or upgradeToAndCall(newImplementation)
stages.cost: Effects can be combined in one spell
stages.explanation: Impersonating the governor on the pinned fork added a minter and minted 1,000,000 USDS without collateral; a non-ward mint and an unapproved holder burn reverted. The upgrade call accepted the current implementation, proving the authorization gate, while verified source permits another compatible implementation; no hostile replacement was replayed.

stages.title: Redeem the PSM stock
stages.action: UsdsPsmWrapper.buyGem(recipient, gemAmt) takes USDC from the LitePSM pocket at par
stages.cost: Approved USDS balance, no exit fee
stages.explanation: With the pinned exit contracts unchanged, a funded, approved caller exchanged 1,000,000 USDS for 1,000,000 USDC, then drained the remaining 4.390bn USDC in one public call. Above-inventory and empty-pocket exits reverted; the initial 4.391bn USDC equals 61.7% of USDS supply or 37.5% of combined USDS and DAI supply at par.

stages.title: Hold the leftover claim
stages.action: Remaining holders face impaired backing and uncertain exit prices
stages.cost: Loss and recovery are not quantified
stages.explanation: If all pinned LitePSM inventory served existing USDS holders, with no replenishment, new minting or DAI competition, 2.731bn USDS would remain outside that exit; DAI conversion and savings-vault withdrawals create no additional USDC inventory. The reviewed token lacks freeze or seizure functions, but an upgrade can change those protections, and neither the shared book nor eventual recovery was valued.

window.label: Governance response window
window.note: The pinned delay gives voters at least 48 hours to elect a replacement hat and cancel the plan. There is no separate guardian veto; changing the delay itself requires execution through PauseProxy.

defenders.name: The 48-hour delay
defenders.why: The pinned delay enforces at least 172,800 seconds of notice. That permits a governance response, but an uncancelled plan becomes executable by anyone after its scheduled time.

defenders.name: Voting holders
defenders.why: Voters can elect a replacement hat and cancel before execution, including during the 48-hour delay. They need strictly more than the incumbent's live approvals; success and acquisition cost were not established.

defenders.name: Emergency Shutdown Module
defenders.why: At the pin, min is max uint256 in MKR base units, far above even all remaining MKR plus prior stake. The ESM cannot fire under this configuration; governance can still call End directly.

defenders.name: The End shutdown module
defenders.why: Sky marks End deprecated in archived documentation. Pinned reads confirm the ESM and PauseProxy as authorised callers, but do not enumerate every ward; governance's shutdown authority is not an independent veto, and complete settlement was not replayed.

defenders.name: The LitePSM
defenders.why: At the pin, funded callers could drain 4.391bn USDC at par, equal to 61.7% of USDS supply with unchanged exit contracts. Replenishment is not guaranteed, and every USDC sender retains Circle token dependence.

defenders.name: The Vow surplus
defenders.why: Pinned Vow credit was 654.473m DAI against 714.592m recognised debt, a 60.119m deficit. The 228.196m queued debt is already included; max-uint hump and sump prevent its legacy surplus and debt auctions at this state.

defenders.name: Circle
defenders.why: Circle's blacklist capability could stop PSM outflows, including hostile withdrawals, but also block legitimate exits. The fork replay blacklisted the pocket and both swap directions reverted; no issuer intervention or recovery is assumed.

crvusd-curve.title: How does crvUSD break?
crvusd-curve.thesis: Compromised Convex keys could authorize unbacked crvUSD issuance: three bypass vlCVX voting, while one operator-delegate key needs a turnout-dependent poll result.
crvusd-curve.premise: Hypothetical: three of the five signers on Convex's vote-extension Safe, or one ConvexCore operator key, are compromised, coerced, or collude. No such compromise has been observed. Using block 26,138,725 as the vote snapshot, the one-key route needs at least 55.48% poll yes when other veCRV abstains, or 94.31% against all outside opposition; these bounds assume Convex casts within the first 3.5 days, at full weight. Future snapshots need recalculation, and the one-key route also depends on the intact Safe not replacing the caster before its ballot.

stages.title: Open a malicious vote
stages.actor: A holder of at least 2,500 veCRV, outside its proposal cooldown
stages.action: Ownership Voting newVote(script: DAO Agent → Factory admin → set_debt_ceiling(attacker, X))
stages.cost: One transaction
stages.explanation: The public vote can open before or after key compromise, subject to the proposer's balance and cooldown requirements. Its script instructs the DAO Agent to raise a debt ceiling for an attacker-controlled address.

stages.title: Wait out the vote
stages.action: Seven-day vote period runs to completion
stages.cost: 7 days, fully public
stages.explanation: At block 26,138,725, Convex's 54.0798% share makes the Safe route's full-weight yes ballot unbeatable, but execution still waits seven days. After closure, Curve requires yes to exceed 51% of votes cast and 30% of snapshot voting power, or simply 51% of snapshot power; the fork replay confirmed that this shortcut does not permit early execution.

stages.title: Execute and mint
stages.action: executeVote → DAO Agent → Factory admin.execute → set_debt_ceiling(attacker, X) → crvUSD.mint(attacker, X)
stages.cost: One transaction, once the vote period has elapsed
stages.missingDefense: No collateral check, no further timelock
stages.explanation: A ceiling above the recipient's recorded residual mints the difference directly to that address. On a fork from block 26,139,017, the vote script minted 10 million crvUSD to an unregistered plain address after the full seven-day period, with no collateral, recipient allowance or co-signature.

stages.title: Sell into the peg
stages.action: Sell the unbacked crvUSD into liquidity pools, including PegKeeper pairs
stages.cost: Market-dependent; no sale replayed
stages.explanation: The new issuance adds claims without adding collateral, diluting existing backing rather than removing collateral from existing loans. Sales would expose pool liquidity, scrvUSD depositors and LlamaLend lenders to a depeg; no realized sale or price path was simulated.

branches.label: Through the Safe
branches.premise: Hypothetical: three of the five signers on the Safe that owns Convex's vote extension are compromised, coerced, or collude.

stages.title: Take three Safe keys
stages.action: Obtain 3 of 5 signatures on the Safe that owns Convex's vote extension
stages.cost: Off-chain: phishing, coercion, or collusion
stages.explanation: The Safe is a plain 3-of-5 with no guard and no modules, so any three owners can sign any call it is allowed to make.

stages.title: Swap the vote caster
stages.action: VoteDelegateExtension.setDaoOperator(attacker)
stages.cost: One transaction
stages.missingDefense: No hand-off timelock or vlCVX approval
stages.explanation: The extension-owning Safe can immediately replace CurveVoteExecutor with any caster, bypassing its vlCVX tally rule. The Safe can also call revertControl and use the Booster owner wrappers to replace the delegate, so blocking setDaoOperator alone would not close both paths.

stages.title: Vote all veCRV yes
stages.action: DaoVote(voteId, true, true) → Booster → VoterProxy → Voting.vote
stages.cost: One transaction
stages.explanation: The replacement caster votes the whole pooled position at once. The cvxCRV holders whose CRV is locked there cannot withdraw it or redirect its vote.

branches.label: Via ConvexCore
branches.premise: Hypothetical operator-delegate compromise: at block 26,138,725 and full-weight voting, the poll needs at least 55.48% yes if other veCRV abstains, or 94.31% to withstand all outside opposition.

stages.title: Take the operator key
stages.action: Obtain control of the operator EOA 0x947B7742C403f20e5FaCcDAc5E092C943E7D0277
stages.cost: Off-chain compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.explanation: ConvexCore's operators are this EOA, a 3-of-5 Safe and FxGaugeExecutor, and the EOA alone can make Core call either owned contract. At block 26,138,725, its delegated epoch-239 weight was 20,690,663.1 CVX, or 45.8184% of that epoch's 45,157,959.4842 CVX supply, while its own locked balance was zero.

stages.title: Rig a one-day poll
stages.actor: ConvexCore, called by the compromised key
stages.action: ConvexCore.execute(platform, createProposal(start, end, Ownership, curveVoteId)) · ConvexCore.execute(executor, setGuardian(operatorEOA, true))
stages.cost: Two transactions; the one-day poll must close early enough to cast within the Curve vote's first 3.5 days
stages.explanation: ConvexCore owns the platform and executor, so the key can link a poll to the Curve vote and appoint itself guardian, skipping only the 12-hour finalization wait. It cannot replace the executor's fixed pointers, forge holder ballots or skip the poll; the fork run still sent the platform's proportional result.

stages.title: Win the conditional poll
stages.action: DaoVotePlatform.vote(platformProposalId, operatorEOA, 10000, 0)
stages.cost: One transaction; no vlCVX purchase needed
stages.explanation: At block 26,138,725, with the delegate's 20,690,663.1 CVX fixed as the sole yes weight D, maximum no weight is floor(D × (10000 - b) / b) in 18-decimal units: about 36.76705146% of epoch-239 supply for a 5,548-basis-point yes target, or 2.76436013% for 9,431. The first bound assumes other veCRV abstains and the second withstands all outside opposition, both at full Curve weight; direct delegator votes reduce D, and exceeding the second bound removes guaranteed passage, not necessarily passage.

stages.title: Cast the proportional split
stages.action: CurveVoteExecutor.executeDaoVote(platformProposalId) → extension.DaoVoteWithWeights(curveVoteId, yayBps, nayBps, true) → Booster → VoterProxy → Ownership Voting.vote
stages.cost: One transaction after the poll closes; it must land within the Curve vote's first 3.5 days
stages.explanation: The executor uses floor(yes × 10000 / (yes + no)): at block 26,138,725 and full Curve weight, 5,548 yes basis points clears the strict 30% quorum with other veCRV abstaining, while 9,431 exceeds 51% of total voting power regardless of outside opposition. One basis point less fails the respective bound; a fork from block 26,139,382 confirmed that 55.48% lost against 15.2% outside opposition while 94.31% passed.

window.label: Public vote window
window.note: The vote is public for seven days, but the intact Safe's response window on the Core route ends when Convex's ballot lands, potentially just after the one-day poll closes. Counted vlCVX opposition can weaken that ballot; the Safe route bypasses the poll. No independent veto was found in the downstream Voting → Agent → Factory execution path.

defenders.name: Other veCRV holders
defenders.why: They can defeat the weaker ConvexCore poll result. At the pinned share and full weight, the Safe's all-yes ballot or ConvexCore's 94.31% poll yes outvotes them at any turnout; 55.48% does not.

defenders.name: vlCVX holders
defenders.why: At the pin, vlCVX opposition can defeat the Core route's conditional poll result but cannot veto Safe caster replacement. Direct delegator voting reduces the attacker's yes weight; the tested obstruction did not silence undelegated holders.

defenders.name: vlCVX delegators
defenders.why: In the current configuration they can vote directly during a running poll and pull their weight out of a delegate's ballot, but ConvexCore can zero the delegation gas limit and re-sync a holder so that a later direct vote reverts. It is an obstructable defence against the ConvexCore route only, not against the Safe.

defenders.name: Convex's two other signers
defenders.why: On the three-key Safe route, the two remaining owners cannot veto a transaction signed by the compromised majority. Individually they have no authority over the separate Core operator key.

defenders.name: The intact Convex Safe
defenders.why: On the Core route, three intact Safe signers can call setDaoOperator or revertControl before the executor's Curve ballot. The guardian can execute immediately after the one-day poll closes, making last-moment intervention a transaction-ordering race.

defenders.name: Other ConvexCore operators
defenders.why: A remaining Core operator can revoke the compromised key, but that key can revoke the others first. The attacker has the first-mover advantage; revocation does not retract a Curve ballot already cast.

defenders.name: Curve Emergency DAO
defenders.why: The 5-of-9 Emergency DAO can pause PegKeepers, adjust risk parameters and lower debt ceilings, but has no independent veto in the Voting → Agent → Factory path. In the fork replay, lowering the minted recipient's ceiling reverted while it held tokens without a Factory allowance, and the same path could not recover tokens transferred to a third party.

defenders.name: The market
defenders.why: Holders can seek an exit during the seven-day notice window. Actual exit prices depend on buyers, liquidity and market responses, none of which the independent pool quotes model.

falsifiers.condition: The vote extension's owner differs from the recorded Convex Safe
The runtime of the extension, Booster or either Booster owner wrapper changes, or the Booster delegate/owner or either wrapper's owner differs from block 26,138,725
The Safe's threshold differs from three, its owner count differs from five, its guard slot is nonzero, or its module list is no longer empty
ConvexCore's enabled operator set or runtime differs from block 26,138,725
Convex's VoterProxy balance is 51% of total veCRV supply or less at the check's pinned block; this is not a future vote snapshot
The Factory, admin intermediary or crvUSD runtime differs from block 26,139,017, or the recorded Factory admin, intermediary DAO, Factory stablecoin or token minter pointer changes

usdc-circle.title: How does USDC break?
usdc-circle.thesis: A bank-reserve shock outlasts Circle's liquidity and public rescue, leaving holders unable to exit at par.
usdc-circle.premise: Hypothetical: a banking shock traps reserve cash, redemptions queue, and neither Circle nor public authorities restores access before confidence fails. USDC recovered after the March 2023 SVB shock; this tail assumes rescue fails or arrives too late, without estimating its likelihood. No current bank failure, reserve shortfall or redemption suspension is asserted. August's examined reserves included net cash and settlement balances, but the examination did not disclose individual bank exposures.

stages.title: Reserve banks fail
stages.action: A correlated bank failure or legal hold interrupts access to reserve cash
stages.cost: Off-chain shock; size is hypothetical
stages.explanation: Circle's August examination classified $10.60B as net cash and settlement balances, without individual bank shares. The scenario assumes enough cash becomes inaccessible to exceed available liquidity; that is not an observed loss.

stages.title: Cash access stalls
stages.action: Reserve assets cannot all become usable settlement cash immediately
stages.cost: Until bank access or replacement funding resumes
stages.explanation: Circle reported that the 2023 backstop would restore access to $3.3B at SVB. August's examination includes short Treasuries and overnight Treasury-backed repos, but their reported values do not prove uninterrupted payment access.

stages.title: Redemptions meet a gate
stages.action: Submit cash redemption requests through Circle's institutional account and banking channels
stages.cost: Banking and account processing; no measured stress deadline
stages.explanation: Outside the EEA, holders need an eligible Circle Mint account to redeem directly, and Mint currently serves institutions. Terms permit qualifying delays or suspensions; EEA holders have separate MiCA rights, not this same account-only contract.

stages.title: Holders sell the discount
stages.action: Sell USDC into stablecoin pools while cash arbitrage is impaired
stages.cost: Trading fees and price impact
stages.explanation: At Ethereum block 26,139,234, a static 10M USDC sale into Uniswap's USDC/USDT 0.01% pool quotes 9.08M USDT, averaging 0.908 USDT per USDC. This measures isolated pool depth, not a forecast; external arbitrage and liquidity changes are excluded.

stages.title: DeFi inherits the shock
stages.action: USDC holdings and shared exit routes transmit the discount into other positions
stages.cost: Depends on protocol response and reserve recovery
stages.explanation: Sky's LitePSM pocket holds 4.39B USDC, and seven sampled Curve and Uniswap pools hold another 78.54M. Those are measured token holdings, not predicted losses; DAI and USDS share Sky's exposure rather than owning separate copies.

stages.title: The rescue falls short
stages.action: Replacement liquidity, deposit recovery and market buying fail to restore timely par exits
stages.cost: Unspecified; no fixed catastrophe clock
stages.explanation: The Fed, Treasury and FDIC protected SVB depositors in 2023, and USDC recovered. This tail requires that a new rescue is absent, too slow or insufficient; the prior intervention does not establish a standing guarantee.

stages.title: Par exits stay unavailable
stages.action: Sell below par or wait for reserve access and recovery
stages.elapsed: T+days to an unknown recovery date
stages.cost: Discount or prolonged illiquidity; loss depends on recovery
stages.explanation: An access shock can cause prolonged illiquidity without a permanent reserve loss. If reserve losses also exceed replacement funding, holders face impairment; Circle's 2025 filing separately warned that even successful reserve claims could be delayed in issuer insolvency.

window.label: Redemption queue
window.duration: Hours to days; no verified upper bound
window.note: Access restored or sufficient replacement funding supplied during this window arrests the chain. The 2023 intervention did so; no present stress-throughput measurement fixes the deadline.

defenders.name: Circle
defenders.why: Can mobilize accessible reserves, replacement banks and corporate liquidity. Whether those resources cover a correlated cash-access shock is not established by the monthly examination.

defenders.name: Treasury, Fed and FDIC
defenders.why: Full deposit access arrested the SVB route in 2023, and a comparable intervention can arrest this chain. The cited intervention does not promise future coverage or timing to USDC holders.

defenders.name: Market arbitrageurs
defenders.why: Can buy discounted USDC when they expect accessible par redemption. If cash access or recovery is doubtful, pool liquidity and market buying do not themselves restore bank reserves.

defenders.name: Circle transfer controls
defenders.why: The pauser and blacklister can block token transfers but cannot restore bank access. At the pin USDC was unpaused and the LitePSM pocket unblacklisted; local fork replays verified both transfer controls.

falsifiers.condition: Reserve bank deposits and net cash exposure are removed, with independently verified Treasury/repo settlement continuity. Watch: August examination only; unchanged text does not re-decide this condition or test settlement access.
Every non-EEA holder gains enforceable direct redemption without an institutional Circle Mint eligibility gate. Watch: USDC and Mint terms; unchanged text does not re-decide eligibility.

Named bank exposures and tested replacement liquidity establish full coverage of the modeled access loss. Watch: August examination and FY2025 filing; unchanged text does not establish replacement-liquidity adequacy.

A binding standing backstop guarantees timely access to all affected reserve deposits and settlement channels. Watch: USDC/Mint terms and the 2023 federal statement; unchanged text cannot establish current guarantees.

gho-aave.title: How does GHO break?
gho-aave.thesis: Two of three Risk Council keys double a mint bucket and issue 310 million GHO to any address, with no deposit and no delay.
gho-aave.premise: Hypothetical: two of the three signers on Aave's Risk Council Safe lose control of their keys. No compromise or misconduct is alleged. At block 26,139,200, the permissions, full bucket and elapsed cooldown enabled the replayed route.

stages.title: Take two Council keys
stages.action: Obtain 2 of 3 signatures on the Aave Risk Council Safe
stages.cost: Off-chain: phishing, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.explanation: The Safe requires two of three owners and has no guard or modules. Using impersonated owners' on-chain hash approvals, the fork replay rejected one approval and executed with two; no real private keys were used.

stages.title: Double the mint bucket
stages.action: GhoBucketSteward.updateFacilitatorBucketCapacity(mainnet GSM facilitator, 620,000,000 GHO)
stages.cost: One transaction
stages.explanation: At the pin, the bucket was full and its last update was about 119 days earlier. Each call can at most double the current capacity after strictly more than 86,400 seconds; raising capacity mints nothing.

stages.title: Mint to any address
stages.action: GhoDirectFacilitator.mint(recipient, 310,000,000 GHO) → GhoToken.mint
stages.cost: One transaction after the cap raise
stages.explanation: The facilitator forwards the chosen recipient and amount without checking a deposit. On the pinned fork, minting 310 million GHO to a fresh address raised supply from 699 million to 1.009 billion without moving collateral.

stages.title: Double again next day
stages.action: Wait strictly more than 24 hours after the increase, then double capacity and mint the new headroom
stages.cost: Two more transactions
stages.explanation: The debounce limits capacity updates, while each mint is limited by unused capacity; neither tracks lifetime issuance. After a further 86,401 seconds, the fork's second doubling and mint brought deposit-free issuance to 930 million GHO.

stages.title: Sell into thin exits
stages.action: Redeem through the mainnet GSM, then sell the remainder into the GHO pools
stages.cost: Minutes
stages.explanation: At block 26,139,200, static quotes covered at least 24.7 million GHO at ≥98% nominal token par, under 8% of the first mint. Venues were quoted independently without rebalancing; this is neither an exhaustive exit ceiling nor a price forecast.

stages.title: Governance arrives late
stages.action: Level-1 payload revokes MINTER_ROLE and zeroes the facilitator's bucket capacity
stages.cost: A new proposal, vote and executor delay
stages.explanation: A newly initiated Level-1 proposal needs a one-day cooldown, three-day vote and one-day executor delay. On the fork, revoking the mint role stopped later issuance without burning existing tokens; the Council's separate capacity-setting permission survived.

stages.title: Holders face dilution
stages.action: Savings depositors, stakers and pool holders remain exposed to the added unbacked issuance
stages.cost: Loss depends on exits and recapitalisation
stages.explanation: The added units have no matching deposit and remain transferable after mint authority is revoked. Holders face dilution unless outside resources cover the loss; neither the eventual price nor recovery is established by the replay.

window.label: Ordinary governance response window
window.note: This assumes a new Level-1 proposal starts when issuance is detected. The measured cooldown, vote and executor delay total five days, allowing repeated capacity increases more than 24 hours apart while the Council retains both permissions.

defenders.name: The third Council signer
defenders.why: One signature cannot block two on a two-of-three Safe that carries no guard and no modules.

defenders.name: Aave governance
defenders.why: A new Level-1 proposal takes at least five days. Revoking the Council's mint role stops this issuance route but leaves its separate steward permission intact; zeroing capacity also stops minting without recovering tokens already issued.

defenders.name: Aave governance guardians
defenders.why: Neither guardian holds any role on the facilitator, the token or the steward at the pinned block, and their cancellation powers sit on proposals and payloads, which this route never uses.

defenders.name: The GHO token
defenders.why: Verified immutable source exposes no pause, freeze, blacklist or administrator clawback; six matching selector probes reverted at the pin. Burning debits the facilitator's own balance, so it cannot retrieve GHO already minted to another address.

defenders.name: stkGHO and Umbrella
defenders.why: The pinned stake was 30.56 million GHO, not outside collateral, and the Core provider's Umbrella registry entry was empty. Neither observation establishes a way to reverse this issuance; any recapitalisation remains outside the replay.

defenders.name: The stablecoin module
defenders.why: Both mainnet modules were unfrozen and unseized at the pin, with quoted inventory for 22.5 million GHO. Freezing conversions closes those exits without revoking the Council's separate mint permission.

defenders.name: The market
defenders.why: Public issuance lets holders try to exit. The sampled quotes cover under 8% of the first mint, but do not establish total market capacity or the price after arbitrage, new liquidity and other trading.

usde-ethena.title: How does USDe break?
usde-ethena.thesis: Five compromised Safe keys can replace USDe's minter after public notice, enabling collateral-free issuance beyond the ordinary mint cap.
usde-ethena.premise: Hypothetical: five governance Safe keys are compromised, a whitelisted executor relays their calls, and no defensive cancellation succeeds during the public delay. No compromise or misconduct is alleged. At Ethereum block 26,139,380, the Safe required five of ten signatures and could schedule a minter replacement with a 24-hour delay. The fork impersonated the Safe and tested its guard separately; it did not reproduce key theft or forge owner signatures.

stages.title: Take five Safe keys
stages.action: Obtain 5 of 10 signatures on the Ethena governance Safe
stages.cost: Off-chain: phishing, coercion, or collusion
stages.explanation: At the pinned block, the Safe required five of ten signatures and had no enabled modules. Its guard accepts this scheduling payload from a whitelisted executor; compromise of the five keys remains hypothetical.

stages.title: Schedule the minter swap
stages.action: TimelockController.schedule(USDe, 0, setMinter(attacker), 0, salt, 86400)
stages.cost: One transaction
stages.explanation: The governance Safe is the only proposer and canceller at the pinned block. Scheduling publishes the target, calldata and delay in a CallScheduled event, making the minter replacement visible before execution.

stages.title: Wait out the delay
stages.action: 24-hour minimum delay before execution
stages.cost: 24 hours, fully public
stages.explanation: The fork rejected early execution and, after cancellation, rescheduling with a shorter delay. Any five Safe owners can authorize cancellation, including the five remaining owners if exactly five keys were compromised; this route assumes they do not stop execution.

stages.title: Execute the swap
stages.action: TimelockController.execute → USDe.setMinter(attacker)
stages.cost: One transaction
stages.explanation: After the delay, the fork executed the queued call and replaced the minter with a plain address while leaving the token owner unchanged. Timelock executor roles are separate from the Safe guard's relay whitelist.

stages.title: Mint without collateral
stages.action: USDe.mint(attacker, amount)
stages.cost: One transaction per batch
stages.explanation: USDe.mint checks the stored minter, with no collateral or economic supply cap. On a fork of block 26,139,380, the replacement issued two billion USDe in one block, ten times the ordinary minter's 200 million per-block cap.

stages.title: Redemption consumes existing backing
stages.action: Eligible users request issuer-quoted redemption
stages.cost: Service availability and pricing unmodelled
stages.explanation: Direct redemption requires eligibility and an issuer quote, with last-look checks. Tokens are fungible: redemption can consume existing backing, but cannot supply the assets missing from additional uncollateralised issuance.

stages.title: Holders face discounted exits
stages.action: Seek secondary-market exits or eligible redemption
stages.cost: Market loss not quantified
stages.explanation: If unbacked issuance overwhelms available backing and demand, holders face discounted exits. The sampled quotes measure only static token outputs at block 26,139,380; the 24-hour sUSDe withdrawal cooldown does not guarantee redemption access or an exit before execution.

window.label: Public 24-hour notice
window.note: The public schedule gives at least 24 hours before execution at the pinned configuration. Early execution and a shorter reschedule reverted on the fork; detection creates no guaranteed liquidity, timely cancellation or holder exit.

defenders.name: Timelocked minter change with a public schedule event
defenders.why: Public notice gives owners time to respond, not holders a guaranteed exit. Only the governance Safe can cancel, using any five owners; shortening the minimum delay itself requires a timelocked operation. From deployment at block 25,301,829 through 26,139,380, its logs contain no direct USDe minter-change schedule and no Cancelled event, not proof of an effective or ineffective off-chain response.

defenders.name: EthenaSafeGuard on the governance Safe
defenders.why: The guard restricts module changes, fallback handlers, delegatecalls and transaction relayers. A separate fork call with the exact scheduling payload passed for a whitelisted executor and reverted for an unwhitelisted address; no independent approval of this minter replacement was required.

defenders.name: EthenaMinting V2 per-block mint cap
defenders.why: At block 26,139,380, the ordinary minter's global mint cap was 200,000,000 USDe per block. The token enforces no such limit: replacing the minter allowed two one-billion-USDe transactions in one fork block, ten times that cap.

defenders.name: Issuer redemption and last-look quoting
defenders.why: Ethena documents eligibility, quotes and last-look checks; its terms limit redemption to a pro-rata reserve share capped at $1, subject to conditions. These controls govern redemption service, not the replacement minter's issuance; the pinned ordinary contract cap was 20 million USDe per block.

defenders.name: sUSDe unstaking cooldown
defenders.why: At block 26,139,380, withdrawing underlying USDe required a 24-hour cooldown. This constrains the wrapper withdrawal route, not secondary sales of sUSDe, and does not ensure that a holder can exit before the minter swap.

defenders.name: Reported backing and off-chain operations
defenders.why: Issuer-reported backing and reserve assets are finite; the token's mint function does not verify them. Ethena's documented hedge and custody services do not impose a token-level issuance cap, and their live loss-absorption capacity was not established.

falsifiers.condition: USDe's owner differs from the recorded Ethena timelock address
The timelock delay falls below 24 hours, its runtime changes, or its live proposer set is no longer exactly the governance Safe
The Safe enables a module, changes guard address, guard runtime or guard owner, or loses the guard's allowed-Safe status
USDe's runtime differs from the reviewed implementation with no token-level issuance cap
A timelock operation containing a direct USDe setMinter call has a Cancelled event attributable to a caller other than the governance Safe

usdt-tether.title: How does USDT break?
usdt-tether.thesis: Three of six issuer keys can immediately redirect Ethereum USDT's settlement logic; direct cash redemption remains gated.
usdt-tether.premise: Hypothetical: three of the six Ethereum issuer-wallet signers are compromised, and a hostile replacement disables settlement before control is recovered. No compromise or misconduct is alleged. This route concerns Ethereum USDT, not an independently verified takeover of every native deployment. A prolonged failure also requires issuer recovery and alternative settlement to fall short; the reserve report does not establish a current shortfall.

stages.title: Take three issuer keys
stages.action: Obtain three confirmations from the six Ethereum issuer-wallet signers
stages.cost: Off-chain compromise; not observed
stages.explanation: The owner is a legacy three-of-six multisig, not a single externally owned account. On a fork, one and two confirmations left the token unchanged; the third executed immediately.

stages.title: Redirect the token
stages.action: submitTransaction(USDT, 0, deprecate(replacement)) → confirmTransaction twice → USDT.deprecate
stages.cost: Three signer transactions, no mandatory wait
stages.explanation: The token accepts the owner's replacement address without checking its interface or enforcing balance preservation. A fork replay through the real multisig activated an intentionally reverting replacement on the third confirmation.

stages.title: Transfers stop settling
stages.action: USDT.transfer → replacement.transferByLegacy → revert
stages.cost: Effective from the redirect transaction
stages.explanation: A subsequent transfer reached the replacement and reverted on the fork. The original contract also delegates balance, allowance and supply reads; its stored balances do not provide an independent usable exit.

stages.title: DeFi settlement is impaired
stages.action: USDT-dependent withdrawals and swaps encounter the same redirected token
stages.cost: Until settlement or integration is repaired
stages.explanation: Aave Core has 2.73B USDT-denominated deposit claims and 84.17M USDT immediately held by its reserve token at the pin. Curve and Uniswap pools share the same token dependency; protocol-level failure propagation is inferred, not replayed end to end.

stages.title: Cash exits remain gated
stages.action: Seek issuer-assisted settlement and direct cash redemption
stages.cost: Verification, issuer processing and redemption fees
stages.explanation: The terms, last updated February 26, 2026, give verified customers personal contractual redemption at $1 per USDT less fees, subject to service suspension under section 6. The fee schedule requires $100,000 minimum redemption and charges the greater of $1,000 or 0.1%; the owner-only redeem function burns issuer inventory without sending dollars.

stages.title: Recovery fails to arrive
stages.action: Wait for issuer recovery or accept impaired secondary-market claims
stages.cost: Unbounded settlement delay; haircut is not measured
stages.explanation: This tail requires issuer recovery and alternative settlement to fall short; multi-chain circulation does not measure their capacity. Settlement failure alone proves neither reserve insolvency nor permanent loss, and pre-shock pool quotes do not guarantee an exit.

window.label: Issuer recovery window
window.note: The third confirmation has no waiting period. A legitimate issuer coalition can compete to restore control and appoint working settlement, but no recovery deadline was established.

defenders.name: Uncompromised issuer signers
defenders.why: While still wallet owners, the remaining three can form a competing threshold coalition, but cannot veto the attacking three. Threshold-approved signer changes can remove that recovery route; success and transaction ordering are not guaranteed.

defenders.name: Token pause and migration
defenders.why: Pause, unpause and replacement selection belong to the same issuer owner. The source permits another replacement, but gives holders no independent rollback; recovery needs issuer control and functioning replacement logic.

defenders.name: Blacklist removal
defenders.why: Removing a blacklist entry does not restore destroyed balances. The fork burned 100,000 USDT and unblacklisting left zero; issuer minting could compensate separately, but no permissionless undo exists.

defenders.name: Verified redemption customers
defenders.why: Verified customers have personal contractual redemption at $1 per USDT less fees, subject to minimums and suspension provisions. That access alone does not repair a token that cannot settle transfers to the issuer.

defenders.name: Reserve assurance and audit
defenders.why: BDO's June 30, 2026 reserve assurance differs from the KPMG FY2025 financial-statement audit Tether announced on August 13, 2026. Neither removes token-admin powers; the underlying KPMG opinion was not reviewed here.

falsifiers.condition: The token owner, three-of-six threshold or signer set differs from the evidence pin, or owner-contract code is absent, requiring fresh review of the captured-authority premise.
The token owner or token/wallet bytecode differs from the source-reviewed immediate redirect path at the pin. Any delay or veto must then be reviewed manually.

Ethereum USDT is deprecated, its replacement address is nonzero, or its bytecode differs from the pinned legacy contract. Replacement compatibility and independent settlement then require fresh review.

Tether's published terms establish a tested independent recovery guarantee for timely settlement despite issuer-threshold capture. The document watch flags text changes only; an unchanged fingerprint does not establish or re-decide that guarantee.

Tether's published terms and fee schedule provide every holder direct cash redemption without verified-customer eligibility or a minimum amount. The document watch flags text changes only; an unchanged fingerprint does not re-decide eligibility.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: How does USD1 break?
usd1-world-liberty-financial.thesis: One minter key can issue USD1 without a supply cap or mint checker; three Safe keys can replace the token's logic.
usd1-world-liberty-financial.premise: Hypothetical: an attacker controls the Ethereum minter's signing key or three of the five signers controlling token upgrades. No compromise or misconduct is alleged or observed. Ethereum block 26,139,384 and BNB Chain block 126,221,941 show plain externally owned minters, no supply cap and a zero mint checker. Minting remains subject to role, recipient, transfer and arithmetic checks. The two Ethereum routes are independently authorized; their shared sale, redemption pressure and loss are hypothetical, not an end-to-end replay.

stages.title: Take issuance or upgrade control
stages.action: Control the minter key or three ProxyAdmin Safe signers
stages.cost: Off-chain key compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.explanation: The assumed compromise targets either one minting address or a separate three-signature upgrade authority. Neither route requires the other's permission; off-chain key custody and compromise feasibility are unverified.

stages.title: Sell into thin pools
stages.action: Sell newly minted or seized USD1 into available liquidity
stages.cost: Minutes
stages.explanation: At BNB Chain block 126,221,941, the sampled USD1/USDT pool quotes 2,636,114 USDT for 5M USD1, averaging 0.5272 USDT per USD1, 47.3% below one-for-one. This assumes unchanged liquidity, active transfers and no external arbitrage or routing; it is not a market-price forecast or proof that an Ethereum attacker reaches BNB liquidity.

stages.title: Par exit needs an account
stages.action: Seek direct redemption as a registered BitGo client in good standing
stages.cost: Eligibility review, fees, and transaction limits
stages.explanation: BitGo's fiat-coin terms target initiating payment typically within two business days after a compliant request, including completed compliance review, rather than guaranteeing cash arrival. Non-clients lack direct redemption access, and transaction limits or suspension can constrain eligible clients.

stages.title: Attempt emergency containment
stages.action: Try freezing affected wallets or pausing transfers
stages.cost: One governor transaction per action
stages.explanation: Under the pinned logic, fork calls immediately froze a 300M-USD1 Ethereum wallet and paused transfers; attempted transfers then reverted. These controls do not undo issuance or guarantee containment after an upgrade, because replacement logic can bypass them.

stages.title: Holders carry the loss
stages.action: Bear losses if recovery or reserve replenishment falls short
stages.cost: Recovery time and final loss unmeasured
stages.explanation: Unbacked issuance creates a supply gap unless reserves are replenished or the extra tokens are recovered; seized balances create a separate loss for their owners. Holders and venues bear any unrecovered loss, but the replay establishes neither its market size nor its permanence.

branches.label: Through the minter hot wallet
branches.premise: Hypothetically, the Ethereum minter's signing key is compromised. The address also holds the burner role; its off-chain custody protections are not established by its empty on-chain code.

stages.title: Take the hot-wallet key
stages.action: Obtain control of the minter EOA
stages.cost: Off-chain key compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.explanation: The Ethereum minter has empty code at block 26,139,384, so the contract requires one address's signature rather than an on-chain multisig threshold. At BNB Chain block 126,221,941, two minting addresses likewise have empty code; this does not establish how their keys are stored.

stages.title: Mint unbacked supply
stages.action: TokenGovernor.mint(recipient, amount)
stages.cost: One transaction, 89,558 gas on the fork
stages.explanation: At Ethereum block 26,139,384, the checker is zero and the verified mint path has no supply cap, while authorization and transfer checks remain. Impersonating the minter on a fork issued 100B USD1 in one call, raising Ethereum supply from 1.6127B to 101.6127B without adding reserves.

branches.label: Through the ProxyAdmin Safe
branches.premise: Hypothetically, an attacker controls three of the five signers of the Safe that owns the token's ProxyAdmin. This is distinct from controlling the minter address.

stages.title: Take three Safe keys
stages.action: Obtain three of five signatures on the ProxyAdmin owner Safe
stages.cost: Off-chain key compromise, coercion, or collusion; not observed
stages.explanation: At Ethereum block 26,139,384, the Safe requires three of five signatures, has no enabled modules and has a zero guard. All five signers have empty code; their off-chain custody protections are unverified.

stages.title: Replace the token logic
stages.action: ProxyAdmin.upgrade(proxy, implementation)
stages.cost: One ProxyAdmin call; Safe signing gas not measured
stages.explanation: ProxyAdmin accepts an immediate upgrade from its owner Safe and rejects other callers. The fork impersonated that Safe and changed the implementation; it did not collect three signatures or execute through the Safe itself.

stages.title: Rewrite holder balances
stages.action: Seize holder balances and mint extra tokens through replacement logic
stages.cost: Two attacker transactions after the upgrade
stages.explanation: On the Ethereum fork, separate calls through the replacement seized 500M USD1 from a wallet holding 624.4M and minted another 1B USD1. Neither required a token role or holder consent, although both transactions were signed by their sender.

window.label: From compromise to attempted containment
window.note: Minting and upgrading have no mandatory on-chain wait. Market transmission, redemption pressure and incident response are assumed sequences, not measured durations; freezing may occur before redemption requests.

defenders.name: Mint checker
defenders.why: The checker address is zero at both chain pins, so no external checker validates backing before minting. Role, recipient and transfer checks still apply.

defenders.name: Safe thresholds
defenders.why: The upgrade Safe needs three of five signatures; the governor-admin Safe needs three of six. Neither has enabled modules or a guard, and neither imposes a transaction delay; the plain minter bypasses both signature thresholds.

defenders.name: Reserve attestation
defenders.why: The monthly examination covers dated reserve snapshots, not continuous backing, and the mint path never reads it. A later shortfall need not appear in the August report.

defenders.name: Freeze and pause roles
defenders.why: Under the pinned logic, authorized freeze and pause calls take effect immediately and can interrupt honest exits. They do not undo completed issuance, and hostile replacement logic can bypass them.

defenders.name: Redemption window
defenders.why: Registered clients in good standing can request redemption at par less fees. Fiat-coin terms target payment initiation typically within two business days after a compliant request, subject to limits and possible suspension.

falsifiers.condition: On Ethereum or BNB Chain, the token's governor, mint-role membership or members' code sizes differ from that chain's evidence pin, requiring review of the plain-address minting route.

On either chain, the governor, governed-token address, implementation, checker or proxy/governor/implementation bytecode changes from its pin. The check detects mint-path drift, not whether changed code actually introduces a cap.

On either chain, ProxyAdmin ownership/code or its Safe's threshold, owners, owner code sizes, modules, guard, singleton or Safe/singleton bytecode differs from the pin, requiring fresh review of immediate upgrade authority.

On either chain, the mint path or mint/freeze/pause role-holder membership, code or recorded Safe/clone protections changes from the pin. The check flags protection drift; it does not measure a newly introduced delay.

BitGo's USD1 Terms or Coin Minting & Redemption Services Terms and Public Terms change. The document watch flags text drift for manual reassessment of universal par redemption; it does not decide eligibility.

lusd-liquity.title: How does LUSD break?
lusd-liquity.thesis: A wrong fallback enables borrowing against overstated ETH and underpays redemptions; sustained borrowing can exhaust Liquity's collateral buffer.
lusd-liquity.premise: Hypothetical: Chainlink stops returning a usable ETH price while the Tellor fallback supplies a valid, fresh but wrong number. No compromise or misconduct is alleged. State and fork examples use Ethereum block 26,139,200 on 2026-10-07; the examples are separate tests, not consecutive transactions. Oracle outputs were mocked, not obtained by compromising either feed. Dollar valuations assume the pinned Chainlink price of $2,617.6773/ETH is the honest market price; they are not forecasts.

stages.title: Primary feed breaks
stages.action: latestRoundData() stops returning a usable answer
stages.cost: Outside the protocol; not observed
stages.explanation: Chainlink answered $2,617.6773/ETH at the pin, with Liquity using its primary feed. The fork instead made the answer revert; unusable or over-four-hour-old primary data sends the pricing logic toward the fallback.

stages.title: Fallback becomes the price
stages.action: PriceFeed.fetchPrice() → _storeTellorPrice(tellorResponse)
stages.cost: One transaction, by anyone
stages.explanation: With Chainlink reverting, one fork call adopted a fresh mocked Tellor value of $260/ETH instead of the stored $2,603.3351, without bounding the jump. Liquity's caller retrieves the newest Tellor value without adding a dispute waiting period.

stages.title: Borrow against overstated ETH
stages.action: BorrowerOperations.openTrove(maxFee, LUSDAmount, upperHint, lowerHint)
stages.cost: One transaction, plus the collateral deposited
stages.explanation: At a mocked $26,176.77/ETH, approximately ten times the pinned Chainlink price, depositing 1,000 ETH credited the borrower with 22.76 million LUSD. The deposit was worth $2.62 million at that reference price, or 11.5 cents per LUSD received; this chosen borrowing amount is not a mint ceiling.

stages.title: Redemption returns less ETH
stages.action: TroveManager.redeemCollateral(...) at the fallback price
stages.cost: One redemption transaction, plus its fee
stages.explanation: In a separate replay at $5,235/ETH, approximately twice the reference price, redeeming 100,000 LUSD returned 18.97 ETH after fees, worth $49,658 at pinned Chainlink prices. That is 49.7 cents per LUSD, versus 99.3 cents in the honest-price control; neither is a market-price forecast.

stages.title: Sell through measured liquidity
stages.action: Swap the new LUSD through the Curve LUSD/3CRV pool
stages.cost: Execution timing and proceeds unmodelled
stages.explanation: The pinned Curve LUSD/3CRV pool quoted five million LUSD for 5,004,346 USDC, assuming unchanged pool state and no arbitrage replenishment. Only that pool exceeded 500,000 LUSD in the bounded two-Curve-pool and twelve Uniswap pair/fee census; balances do not establish executable depth or exclude other venues.

stages.title: Borrowing exhausts the buffer
stages.action: Repeated borrowing leaves less collateral than debt
stages.cost: 10,000 ETH in the counterexample
stages.explanation: Ten 1,000-ETH deposits at the same approximately tenfold false price left 84.4787% collateralisation at the assumed honest-price reference. Damage scales with the mispricing window and borrowing volume; the starting buffer absorbs shocks but guarantees no backing floor.

window.label: While the wrong number is live
window.duration: Until accepted oracle data corrects the price
window.note: The last five Tellor publications at the pin were about four hours apart; the latest was 3h 10m old, within the four-hour limit. Expiry freezes the last accepted price rather than shutting down.

defenders.name: Chainlink primary feed
defenders.why: In the pinned primary-working state, a mocked $260 fallback left the fetched price at $2,617.6773 and liquidation reverted. Merely answering is insufficient: invalid, stale or sharply diverging Chainlink rounds can still trigger fallback logic.

defenders.name: Overcollateralisation
defenders.why: The pinned 720.6% ratio uses the stored last-good price; Chainlink-valued backing was 724.6%. One replayed deposit left 391.5%; ten left 84.5%, so the buffer absorbs initial shocks but cannot cap sustained false-price borrowing.

defenders.name: Immutability
defenders.why: Liquity's reviewed contracts have no privileged mint, pause or upgrade path; their owners are renounced. External oracle administration is separate, and nobody inside Liquity can override a wrong price.

defenders.name: Price-feed recovery rule
defenders.why: On a price-fetching transaction, valid, fresh feeds within 5% (difference divided by the lower price) restore Chainlink. Restoring Chainlink alone is insufficient; a stale fallback can leave the last adopted wrong price in use.

defenders.name: Recovery-mode liquidation limits
defenders.why: At $260/ETH, recovery-mode liquidation closed 69 of 70 vaults but offset only 68,878 LUSD, leaving 717.1% backing at pinned Chainlink prices. The last vault cannot be liquidated; redemption reverts below 110% oracle-valued system collateralisation.

defenders.name: Liquity V2 shutdown path
defenders.why: A stale stETH-USD feed irreversibly shut down the newer protocol's wstETH borrowing branch on the fork, while retaining a redemption path. Liquity V1 has no equivalent shutdown mechanism.

exposure.label: LUSD outstanding
exposure.detail: 26,101,419.74 LUSD, matching the protocol's own entire system debt at the pinned block.

exposure.label: Collateral behind it
exposure.detail: 72,251.2195 ETH across 70 loan vaults, called Troves, at the pin; a 720.6% collateral ratio at the stored last-good price of $2,603.3351/ETH.

exposure.label: Stability Pool depth
exposure.detail: At the pin, 7,568,151.33 LUSD and 591.62 ETH; LUSD deposits equal 29.0% of entire system debt. Recovery-mode vaults at or below 100% collateralisation redistribute debt without first using these deposits.

exposure.label: Measured exit
exposure.detail: At the pin, Curve LUSD/3CRV held 2,257,071 LUSD and BOLD/LUSD held 190,629 LUSD. Twelve Uniswap v3 LUSD pair/fee combinations with USDC, USDT and WETH at fees 100/500/3000/10000 yielded nine deployed pools, each below 2,000 LUSD; no global census was performed. Curve quoted 5 million LUSD for 5,004,346 USDC without replenishment or routing; BOLD/LUSD quotes reverted at every size tested, which does not prove zero liquidity.

exposure.label: Repeated-mint counterexample
exposure.detail: At fork block 26,139,200, ten consecutive 1,000-ETH deposits at the same mocked $26,176.77/ETH, approximately tenfold, each credited a borrower with 22.76 million LUSD. System debt reached 254.866 million LUSD against 82,251.2195 ETH, or 84.4787% collateralisation, assuming pinned Chainlink's $2,617.6773/ETH is the honest market price. The replay supplied 10,000 ETH, held the false price constant and made no market sales; it establishes a backing shortfall under those assumptions, not sale proceeds or attack cost.
